A Reply To Josiah About The Medical Marijuana "Scam" -- Demanding A Retraction and an Apology

Dear Josiah:

I am Richard Cowan, the former National Director Of NORML.

You are perpetuating one of the more absurd prohibitionist scams by claiming on your web site that I have said that the medical marijuana movement is a "scam." I have never said any such thing.

Moreover, this false attribution, which contradicts my well-known and widely published beliefs, is defamatory and constitutes libel in that it portrays me as an unconscionable liar who is viciously manipulating the public as well as seriously ill and disabled people.

Your posting of this on your web site without attempting to authenticate it constitutes a flagrant and reckless disregard for the truth. Therefore, I hereby demand that you remove it and all references to it from your site and that you post a corrected version of my views along with a formal apology for this libel.

Your failure to comply promptly will cause me to turn the matter over to my attorneys for the appropriate legal action. I hope that this will not be necessary and that you will realize that you have violated the 9th Commandment by libeling me and that you will want to make amends.

As for my actual statement, I was speaking extemporaneously, but the following is what I think is an accurate but somewhat abbreviated transcript:

"The key to it (full legalization) is medical access. Because, once you have hundreds of thousands of people using marijuana medically, under medical supervision, the whole scam is going to be blown. I mean what we know is that marijuana prohibition is the greatest fraud ever perpetrated on the American people...

The consensus here is that medical marijuana is our strongest suit. It is our point of leverage which will move us toward the legalization of marijuana for personal use, and in that process we will begin to break down the power of the narcocracy to wage a war of terror over things.

And so I think that we have the beginning with medical marijuana, then the legalization of personal use, and then we are in a position to take on the narcocracy on all of its abuses across the board, including obviously LSD and the psychedelics and the inhumane treatment of hard drug addicts as well."

This version comes from a prohibitionist web site put up by the Lt. Governor of Washington and paid for by the Federal government’s High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area funds. Its source is the very prohibitionist Sue Rusche of Atlanta’s National Families In Action. In short, you are not taking my word for it.

You can find this on line at http://www.mfiles.org/legalization_spin/b3_org_trends.html

Also, for the record, the conference was about medical marijuana and about observing – not celebrating -- the 50th anniversary of the discovery of LSD. If it had been about only LSD, as the National Director of NORML, I would not have been there.

So that you will not think that I am hiding anything, I have long been on record favoring the complete legalization of marijuana. In fact, I have no hidden agendas. I was actually explaining that our support for medical marijuana was not a departure from my long-standing support for full legalization. I think that medical marijuana is a worthy goal in itself, because I think that it is especially immoral to arrest sick people who find that marijuana helps them. But, yes, I also think that it will lead to full legalization for reasons that I will explain below.

Now the libel laws and the 9th Commandment aside, which is where you seem to have left them, stop and think for a minute. Consider the following points:

  1. Can you imagine the head of a movement getting up at a public meeting and describing his movement’s position as a "scam?" This makes no sense at all. That alone should have caused you to question to authenticity of this "quote."
  2. Even if I had said that, and sometimes people do misspeak, that would not necessarily reflect my views. After all, I have written extensively on the subject, so taking such a quote out of context would prove nothing. It would be cute for a rhetorical zinger, but nothing more -- without being unethical and libelous.
  3. Even if I did say it and actually believed this nonsense, that would still not prove that is was true. No one person controls the medical marijuana movement, and medical marijuana has the support of many medical groups, including the California Medical Association. The editor of the New England Journal of Medicine has called for immediate medical access in a scathing editorial. Did I "scam" all of these people? Or are they all a part of this "scam?" Crypto-druggies?
  4. Think about the substance for a moment. How would having "hundreds of thousands of people using marijuana medically, under medical supervision" lead to the full legalization of marijuana, if marijuana is as dangerous as you say it is? This year the FDA has had to recall a number of drugs that it had previously approved, because having them used by large numbers of people under medical supervision proved them to be very dangerous. Indeed, the surest way to find out the truth about marijuana will be to have it widely used under medical supervision. I think that marijuana will be proven to be very useful medically, with very few side effects, and this will result in the discrediting of the fraud, scam, deceit, cruelty, sham, shame of marijuana prohibition. Even if marijuana turned out to be terribly dangerous, it could still be medically useful, but it would certainly not be the way to "scam" the public into legalizing it for non-medical use.

The point of all this is that the statement attributed to me is so patently absurd that I cannot imagine your making it the centerpiece of your web site. You seem to have based your arguments for marijuana prohibition around this ridiculous statement and what it implies about the marijuana reform movement.

I hope that your recognition that this statement is itself a scam -- and that you have been deceived by sources that you trusted -- will cause you to reconsider your views.

However, at the very least, I think that you should recognize that those of us who oppose marijuana prohibition do so out of honestly held beliefs. We do not love children any less than you. We simply think that marijuana prohibition is counterproductive and it is making the substance abuse problems even worse. You may disagree, but disagree with what we are actually saying, not some nonsense made up by an over zealous prohibitionist.

If you want to more fully explore my actual views, I also have a web site www.marijuananews.com 

I look forward to your prompt removal from your site of the libelous misrepresentation of my views and the posting of my actual statement with an appropriate apology.

After that, I challenge you to an exchange of views. I will publish a statement by you on my site. I dare you to reciprocate by making your readers aware that there are actual humans who disagree with you.

Sincerely,

Richard Cowan

Marijuananews.com
